About the Project

Cambridge's sensor technologies CDT supports research in sensing and its applications in an uncertain world. Applicants follow the programme's admission guidance and the Cambridge course funding process, with selection for funded places managed through the doctoral training route.

Research Areas

  • Sensor technologies
  • Engineering
  • Data and measurement

About University of Cambridge

Cambridge offers research degrees through its departments and colleges. Doctoral training programmes in sensors, environmental science and cardiovascular research have their own selection and funding arrangements alongside university admission.

Official details: Read the programme or project information

Application route: Follow the official application instructions

2026/27 UKRI reference rate: the minimum UKRI doctoral stipend is £21,805 per year, tax-free (London institutions +£2,000), effective 1 October 2026.

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the deadline: 6 January 2027 (funding deadline). Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.
